2 Thessalonians 3:17 Benediction

Paul is seeking God's blessing for his
church. He does this through prayer (chapter 1)
In the epistle, the audience is the church,
so he cannot write a prayer addressing God directly.
He is communicating w/ the people, not God. But
he is indeed praying in a sense: 1 Thessalonians
5 and 2 Thessalonians 3:17 - he breaks into
prayer.

Numbers 6 sees the High Priest and his
sons are told to say the Aaronic blessing and
to do so in perpetuity. This blessing was
said to "put God's Name" upon his people.

Luke 24 after the resurrection Jesus
ascends into heaven. Before doing so, he lifts
his hands to bless his people.

Genesis 27 Calvin teaches whatever the heralds
of salvation proclaim will surely come to pass insofar
as the message as it has its foundation in
God. The benediction, then, is from God rather
than men.

Psalm 3 God is the "lifter of my head"

We live expectantly. Hoping for his return. Trusting
in his "good hand" upon us.

cards.text: While addressing the congregation rather than speaking directly to God, the apostle breaks into prayer to seek God's blessing on the church.
put God's Name" upon his people.
Before ascending to heaven after the resurrection, Jesus lifted His hands to bless His people.
Because the heralds' message is founded in God, the benediction comes from God rather than men.
lifter of my head
good hand" upon us.

results.transcript:
MATTHEW 5:9; 43-48

"Blessed are the peacemakers for they shall
be called sons of God"

INTRO The posture and disposition of strength
is to seek and desire peace. We are
war-makers. Strife, division and conflict
are the air we breathe.

We have eternal, internal peace w/ God. We are
called to bring peace to those around us.
Those who think highly of themselves (rich in
spirit) do not make peace. We make great
strife. Sinners are at war w/ God. The gospel
is a message of peace. The gospel is the foundation
of peace: it makes peace, but is not peace keepg.
The strife of this life does not come from
the gospel. People hate the gospel. Not because it
is wrong but b/c they are at enmity w/ Christ.
We identify issues that are not places for
conflict: preference, not w/r/t truth.
Love the difficult people. Ps 86:5 God is
ready to forgive.

cards.text: The posture and disposition of strength is to seek and desire peace.
Strife, division and conflict are the air we breathe.
Because believers have eternal peace with God, they are called to bring peace to those around them.
Those who are proud do not make peace, but instead create strife.
The gospel is the foundation of peace: it makes peace, but is not peace keepg.
Opposition to the gospel arises not from error in the message, but from hostility toward Christ.
Believers should avoid conflict over personal preferences rather than matters of truth, and love difficult people.

results.transcript:
Rules for Walking in Fellowship (John Owen)

Psalm 1 is our aim: to be the blessed
man who "meditates" upon God's Law. We
see it as "not burdensome" and as a
"delight."

1. Sincere, affectionate and genuine love for one another
love is the fulfilling of the law. "Love is the
fountain of all our duties concerning God and
man." (John Owen) This is one way in
which men are drawn to Christ. Love consists
in relishing the sight of seeing folks as
blessed.
2. Unity in general and in particular
Forgiveness, humility, to those who are difficult.
3. Encouragement and edification
Exhorting one another
4. Admonishment and watchfulness
This should apply first of all to ourselves. We
should also make it abundantly clear that
our concern is the glory of Christ and
to good of our neighbor.

"Hiding, removing, covering offenses is from the
footsteps of Christ..."

cards.text: Our aim is to be blessed people who meditate on God's law, viewing it not as burdensome but as a delight.
Sincere, affectionate, and genuine love fulfills the law and draws people to Christ.
Love is the fountain of all our duties concerning God and man.
Love consists in relishing the sight of seeing others blessed.
Maintain unity through forgiveness and humility toward those who are difficult.
Encourage and edify one another through mutual exhortation.
Admonishment and watchfulness must start with ourselves, motivated by the glory of Christ and our neighbor's good.
Hiding, removing, covering offenses is from the footsteps of Christ...

results.transcript:
MALACHI: Chapter One: 2-5

INTRO Israel is waiting for freedom and
a King. They had been restored to the land,
but are still under the thumb of a foreign King.
They were waiting for the Dynasty of David.
Waiting gives way to doubt and then despondency.
The Grounds of Gods Covenant Love
"I have loved you" says the Lord... But Israel
responds in contrariness. They expected God to
fulfill their felt needs. But God's love comes
through his unconditional election: Deuteronomy 7:6
for example, or also consider the person of Jacob.
Genesis 34 - Ephesians 1. This should create
wonder in worship, zeal in our service and perspective
in our trials
The Proof of God's Covenant Love
This is found in Jacob and Esau. Esau is
cut off. Even though Jacob was brought near.
God says: look at Edom, look at Esau, He shows
his love by fierce opposition to his enemies.
Those embraced by the covenant of God's
choosing are greatly loved. John 3:17 those who
are unbelieving are outside the covenant and
"condemned already."
The Assurance of God's Covenant Love

cards.text: Israel was waiting for freedom and a king, but waiting gave way to doubt and despondency.
I have loved you
God's covenant love is rooted in unconditional election rather than in fulfilling felt needs.
Understanding God's election produces wonder in worship, zeal in service, and perspective in trials.
God proves His covenant love through His choice of Jacob over Esau and His opposition to His enemies.

results.transcript:
PSALM 98: Congregational Singing to the
Glory of God

Singing is an expression of our unity in Christ.
"...sing... for he has done marvelous things!" A silent
Christian appears to be unbelieving regarding these
things. They would otherwise be compelled - in the
marvel of it - to sing. "His right hand and
holy arm have worked salvation for him. The Lord
has made known his salvation; he has revealed
his righteousness in the sight of the nations." This
is a rich declaration of God's "marvelous" works.
It is the "marvel" of God's work which elicits
our songs. "He has remembered," not us, "his steadfast
love and faithfulness to the house of Israel. All the
ends of the earth have seen the salvation of
our God."
I. We are commanded to sing because he knows what
we need. Acts 16:25 shows God's design for our songs to
be triumphant. It is a great witness and encourgment
to see and hear others sing.

cards.text: Singing serves as a vital expression of believers' unity in Christ.
A silent Christian appears to be unbelieving regarding these things. They would otherwise be compelled - in the marvel of it - to sing.
It is the "marvel" of God's work which elicits our songs.
God commands us to sing because He knows our needs, designing song to be a triumphant witness and encouragement to others.

results.transcript:
Triumph of the Lamb 09/20/2020
Revelation 1:1-3

The book of Revelation was given to the Church to assure her Christ is sovereign over world history and, in the end, he is exalted as a triumphant King over the new creation. God knows it often feels like Satan is winning. The revelation is from God the Father, to Jesus Christ and
(1) Preterist View: the book is already fulfilled
(2) Futurist View: the fulfillment entails a literal thousand year reign of Christ, rapture, and so on
(3) Historicist View: a chronological view of Church History
(4) Idealist View: encouragement for spiritual warfare

Rev 13 and the beast
- (1) sees him as Roman emperor
(2) sees him as antichrist
(3) sees him as the Pope
(4) sees him as govt in any age

With (1), we do see the revelation was given for the first century churches; (2) it speaks to the end of times; (3) it is relevant to all history

The book cites the OT over 500x - more than all the New Testament books combined.

Three foundational themes of Revelation
(1) The Victory and Reign of Christ
It is the great testimony of Christ; Rev 1:5-9, Rev 19
(2) The Church is in a Spiritual Battle
Things are not always as they appear. There is a great spiritual war, which we can only see the effects. Satan is both a lion w/ a roar and a serpent with a slither. The imagery of Revelation shows the world as it truly is: for example, the nations and armies are doomed to destruction but the suffering Church is destined for glory.
(3) They are blessed who hear + keep Revelation
There is a great blessing to listen to this book. To "keep" it no matter the cost: our lives, wealth, etc... there is a great blessing.

cards.text: Revelation was given to assure the Church that Christ is sovereign over world history and will be exalted as triumphant King over the new creation.
The four views of Revelation each capture an aspect of truth: it spoke to first-century churches, speaks to the end of times, and remains relevant throughout all history.
The book cites the OT over 500x - more than all the New Testament books combined.
Revelation's first foundational theme is the victory and reign of Christ as the great testimony of Christ.
The Church is engaged in a spiritual war where earthly powers face destruction while the suffering Church is destined for glory.
Satan is both a lion w/ a roar and a serpent with a slither.
There is a great blessing promised to those who listen to Revelation and keep it regardless of the cost.

Gospel Partnership
08.16.20
Philippians 4:14-20
Yet it was kind of you to share my trouble. And you Philippians know that in the beginning of the gospel, when I left Macedonia, no church entered into partnership with me in giving and receiving, except you only. Even in Thessalonica you sent me help for my needs once and again. Not that I seek the gift, but I seek the fruit that increases to your credit. I have received full payment, and more. I am well supplied, having received Epaphroditus the gifts you sent, a fragrant offering a sacrifice acceptable and pleasing to God. And my God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus. To our God and Father be glory forever and ever.

I. A Partnership which bears one another's burdens
Not just "writing checks" but encouraging one another.
"Sharing our troubles." This is a great blessing of being a Christian.
II. Sacrificial Giving
The church at Philippi was the only one which supported Paul. God accepts and is pleased w/ our giving.
- God promises to provide our every need
III. Motives for God's glory
We give for the right purposes. To see God's glory.

cards.text: True gospel partnership is not merely writing checks, but sharing troubles, encouraging one another, and bearing each other's burdens.
This is a great blessing of being a Christian.
God accepts and is pleased with sacrificial giving, and He promises to supply our every need.
Our giving should be driven by the right motives: to see God's glory.

A Tale of Two Prayers 08.16.20
Luke 18:9-14 "God be merciful to me, a sinner"

At creation, Genesis 3, we see God created man for fellowship with himself. But Adam and Eve believed God witheld from them and trusted in Satan. He did not leave them w/o hope for reconciliation.

Jesus told this parable "to those who trusted they themselves were righteous." The two men are total opposites. Based on appearances, it seemed like the Pharisee was right w/ God.

The Pharisees Prayer: compares himself to others. This is similar to todays rhetoric where everyone is comparing themselves and degradation of others in anger. Reviling, being self righteous happens constantly online. He also refers to himself in self-reliance w/o giving any expression of a need for God at all.

The Tax collector's Prayer: A humble and contrite approach to God is fundamental. This approach to God is of the essence of Christian faith. His prayer - in greek - says "the sinner" and the word for mercy is from atonement.

cards.text: God be merciful to me, a sinner
God created man for fellowship with Himself and did not leave humanity without hope for reconciliation after the fall.
to those who trusted they themselves were righteous.
The Pharisee relied on himself and compared himself to others without expressing any need for God.
A humble and contrite approach to God is fundamental and essential to the Christian faith.

Acts 4:18, 20 "They called them and charged them not to speak or teach in the name of Jesus... But Peter and John answered them "Whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you rather than to God, you must judge, for we cannot but speak of what we've seen and heard.

results.transcript:
MARK 4:33-41 : An Fearful Circumstance       07/26/20
Rev Ross Hodges
It is a common exhortation: do not fear. Isaiah 41,
MATTHEW 5, etc... We are told to not be anxious and not
to fear. In circumstances that are hard, we can be taught
to trust rather than fear.
I. A Right View of Discipleship (v37) "And a great
windstorm arose and waves were filling the boat." Jesus tells
them "Let us go across to the other side."
Once the storm arose the disciples must've become
bewildered: "Why did he lead us here? Did he not know
this storm would come?" The truth is, we learn much by
affliction. We long for heaven. "It was good for me I was
afflicted. This is essential to discipleship
II. A Right View of Christ (v38) "Teacher, do you not care
that we are perishing?" This is an absurd question. He is
in the boat, indeed, on the earth precisely because he
cares. Being exhausted, beaten, tortured. Jesus is God w/ us.
He loves us. He needs only to raise his voice.

cards.text: In hard circumstances, believers can be taught to trust God rather than fear.
Learning through affliction is essential to discipleship and makes us long for heaven.
The truth is, we learn much by affliction. We long for heaven.
Jesus is present with us and suffered on earth precisely because He cares and loves us.
He is in the boat, indeed, on the earth precisely because he cares.
